key_insight: A Convolutional LSTM autoencoder can learn compact, unsupervised representations that jointly capture spatial structure and spectral (wavelength) dependencies in Integral Field Spectroscopy (IFS) data across 19 optical emission lines, enabling discovery and downstream analysis without labels.
problem_solved: High-dimensional IFS cubes contain rich spatial and spectral correlations but lack large labeled datasets; this work addresses how to learn generalized spatio‑spectroscopic features unsupervised so models can summarize, compare, and discover patterns in galaxy data.
method: Treat IFS data as spatio‑spectral sequences (spatial maps across wavelength channels) and preprocess into multi‑channel input cubes covering 3800–8000 Å across 19 emission lines.

Use a Convolutional Long Short‑Term Memory (ConvLSTM) autoencoder: convolutional layers extract spatial features per channel while ConvLSTM units model sequential spectral dependencies, compressing into a low‑dimensional latent representation.
Train unsupervised with a reconstruction objective to produce embeddings useful for clustering, anomaly detection, and transfer to supervised downstream tasks.
impact: Provides a scalable pretraining approach for high‑dimensional spatio‑spectral data that reduces dependence on labels, yields interpretable latent maps for scientific discovery, and can be adapted to other domains with spatial + spectral/temporal structure.
visual_elements: Architecture diagram: Conv + ConvLSTM encoder → latent bottleneck → ConvLSTM + Conv decoder (show data flow and shapes).
Input IFS cube panel: spatial RGB slices across representative emission lines and wavelength axis to show the 3D nature of the data.
Latent embedding visualization: UMAP/t‑SNE of learned embeddings colored by galaxy properties or spectral class to show clustering/separation.
Reconstruction comparison: side‑by‑side original vs reconstructed emission-line maps and representative spectra to demonstrate fidelity.
paper_title: Spatio-Spectroscopic Representation Learning using Unsupervised Convolutional Long-Short Term Memory Networks
paper_authors: Kameswara Bharadwaj Mantha, Lucy Fortson, Ramanakumar Sankar, Claudia Scarlata, Chris Lintott
